title: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling

paper.title: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling
paper.abstract:
Abstract Open-source web agents are now strong enough to execute realistic
browser tasks, but training them with reinforcement learning still
depends on weak supervision: binary task success is too sparse for
credit assignment, while frontier-language-model judges are too
expensive to call at every step and cannot be assumed available at
deployment. We introduce CLIFT, a training and test-time scaling
method built around conformal self-verification. During training,
the agent answers natural-language verification questions about its
own rollouts; a Compositional Conformal Certifier keeps only
question signals whose URL-conditional evidence agrees with a
training-time judge, assigns signed trust weights through
polarity-aware lift, and blends the resulting verifier score into
per-step rewards in a way that never subtracts from the judge
baseline. At test time, the same certified bank is frozen and reused
as structured evidence for Conformal Trajectory Selection (CTS): the
agent samples a greedy rollout and one or more diverse retries, the
self-verifier summarises each URL trace, and a conservative
majority-vote rule chooses whether to swap away from the current
incumbent without calling any external judge. This single mechanism supports three
settings. On WebArena Infinity, CLIFT achieves state-of-the-art
performance among open-source web agents. On VisualWebArena, a
bank trained with the open model transfers to GPT-5.5 at test time
and reaches state-of-the-art performance under the canonical
harness. On Online Mind2Web, without training an agent on the
benchmark, translating the certified question bank improves a
live-web agent in zero-shot evaluation. Together these results
position conformal self-verification as a way to turn costly judge
feedback into a reusable training signal and a judge-free
test-time scaling signal.

Learn more × Back to arXiv License: CC BY 4.0 arXiv:2610.06829v1 [cs.CL] 05 Oct 2026 CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling Yifan Zhang Yutong Dai Viraj Prabhu Zhiyuan Hu Ran Xu Zeyuan Chen Affiliation: Salesforce AI Research Affiliation: { yifan.zhang , yutong.dai , viraj.prabhu }@salesforce.com Affiliation: { zhiyuan.hu , ran.xu , zeyuan.chen }@salesforce.com Abstract Open-source web agents are now strong enough to execute realistic browser tasks, but training them with reinforcement learning still depends on weak supervision: binary task success is too sparse for credit assignment, while frontier-language-model judges are too expensive to call at every step and cannot be assumed available at deployment. We introduce CLIFT, a training and test-time scaling method built around conformal self-verification. During training, the agent answers natural-language verification questions about its own rollouts; a Compositional Conformal Certifier keeps only question signals whose URL-conditional evidence agrees with a training-time judge, assigns signed trust weights through polarity-aware lift, and blends the resulting verifier score into per-step rewards in a way that never subtracts from the judge baseline. At test time, the same certified bank is frozen and reused as structured evidence for Conformal Trajectory Selection (CTS): the agent samples a greedy rollout and one or more diverse retries, the self-verifier summarises each URL trace, and a conservative majority-vote rule chooses whether to swap away from the current incumbent without calling any external judge. This single mechanism supports three settings. On WebArena Infinity, CLIFT achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source web agents. On VisualWebArena, a bank trained with the open model transfers to GPT-5.5 at test time and reaches state-of-the-art performance under the canonical harness. On Online Mind2Web, without training an agent on the benchmark, translating the certified question bank improves a live-web agent in zero-shot evaluation. Together these results position conformal self-verification as a way to turn costly judge feedback into a reusable training signal and a judge-free test-time scaling signal. 1 Introduction Open-source web agents have reached the point where they can operate realistic browser interfaces, but the verifier remains the bottleneck for improving them with reinforcement learning. A binary success signal is easy to deploy but too sparse for credit assignment: when all rollouts in a GRPO group ( Shao et al., 2024 ) receive the same outcome, the advantage estimate collapses. A frontier language model judge ( Bai et al., 2022 ; Liu et al., 2023 ) provides richer feedback, but it is costly during training and cannot be assumed available at test time. This tension is especially visible in web-agent benchmarks: WAI ( Zhou, 2026 ) uses programmatic per-app verifiers, VWA ( Koh et al., 2024 ) uses outcome-based URL/DOM checks, and live-web suites such as OM2W ( Xue et al., 2025 ) depend on noisy LLM judges. The policy is often not the only limiting object; the way we score and select its rollouts can dominate the observed success rate. Table 1 : Feedback mechanisms for web-agent RL and test-time scaling. Dense = step-level feedback beyond binary outcome; URL = URL-state grounding; Cert. = certified trust; J-free = judge-free test time; TTS = test-time scaling; Xfer = reusable bank transfer. CLIFT maintains a bank of natural-language verification questions about web-agent behaviour and certifies which questions are reliable at which URL states. The same bank is used in two places (Figure 2 ). During training, certified bank evidence is blended with the comparative judge to produce a denser per-step reward and URL-stratified advantages. At test time, the trained agent runs a greedy trajectory plus diverse retries; the frozen certified bank summarizes each URL trace; and a conservative trajectory selector keeps one emitted trajectory per task. The common object is not a new model but a calibrated verifier: a set of questions, URL scopes, polarity signs, and conformal trust weights that can be reused after training. Figure 1 : CLIFT concept. Vanilla GRPO broadcasts one trajectory-scalar reward; CLIFT scores each visited URL with verification questions and inherits the URL score to actions taken there. Full pipeline: Figure 2 . The certifier is the part that makes this more than prompt engineering. Each verification question carries a URL scope and a polarity sign indicating whether YES is evidence of progress or failure. A Mondrian adaptive conformal tracker ( Gibbs and Candès, 2021 ; Vovk, 2012 ) estimates whether that question separates high- and low-judge rollouts at the relevant URL granularity. Certified questions receive signed trust weights. During training this gives a verifier reward that can only add evidence on top of the judge baseline, preventing the reward-collapse failure of earlier linear blends. During test-time scaling, the same signed evidence is frozen and presented to a comparative selector over two completed trajectories. In both cases, the question bank is a compact interface between expensive judge feedback and the agent’s own rollouts. We evaluate this idea in three complementary ways. On WAI, where programmatic verifiers provide dense training supervision, CLIFT improves a trainable open Gemma-4 agent and reaches the strongest public 9-app score we are aware of; the point is both training and CTS on the same open backbone. On VWA, where the evaluation is more outcome-based, we use the bank created during Gemma-4 training as a test-time verifier for GPT-5.5, showing that the learned verification knowledge transfers to a stronger closed backbone and reaches state-of-the-art performance under the canonical harness. On OM2W, we push transfer further: no agent is trained on OM2W; instead, the certified question bank is translated and recalibrated, then used by CTS to improve live-web test-time scaling. These three stories support the same claim: conformal self-verification is useful both as a training signal and as a reusable, judge-free test-time scaling signal. Related work is discussed after the empirical section (§ 6 ). 2 CLIFT: Conformal Lift-calibrated Introspective Filtering of Trajectories Figure 2 : CLIFT overview. Training: rollouts are scored by a comparative judge and by a self-verifier that queries a polarity-tagged question bank. The CCC certifies question weights by URL tier, yielding a signed verifier score that is asymmetrically added to the judge reward and then converted into URL-stratified token advantages. Test-time scaling: the trained agent emits a greedy rollout and diverse retries; the frozen certified bank produces per-URL evidence for each pairwise comparison, and a conservative repeated-vote rule decides whether to keep the incumbent or swap. CLIFT is a GRPO-family policy-gradient method ( Shao et al., 2024 ) that changes how rollouts are scored and reused. It turns natural-language verification questions into a conformally certified URL-aware verifier, uses that verifier to add non-negative per-step evidence during training, and freezes the same bank for CTS at test time. Thus both halves of Figure 2 share one object: questions with URL scopes, polarity signs, and certified trust weights. 2.1 The Conformal Verifier A verification question (VQ) is a YES/NO check on the agent’s behaviour.
